criteria.criterion: docs/design/squash-chain-landing.md gains an Appendix B answering each review-2 finding (R2-M1, R2-m1, R2-m2, R2-m3, R2-n1, R2-n2) with a disposition and the section changed; the review file is unchanged.
criteria.evidence: In the diff, Appendix B has one table row for each of the six findings. Each row gives a disposition (Accepted) and links the section that changed. The review file does not appear in the diff stat.

criteria.criterion: §4.1 defines how the core derives previous_job from the base commit (including after a hand change, a records-only commit, and an unlanded predecessor), states it as an assumption the user may change, and says what is written when none is found.
criteria.evidence: The new §4.1 paragraph 'Where previous_job comes from (R2-M1)' gives the rule: the latest landed job in the base commit's history. It covers a hand change, a records-only commit, an unlanded predecessor, and no job found (field absent). It calls the rule a stated assumption the user may change and labels it (inferred). I checked the rule against run.rs 1145-1195: the core writes the landed outcome when it advances the branch, so stacked jobs on a branch find their predecessor.

criteria.criterion: The design resolves R2-m2: one remaining job is judged by the single-job rule (or the head rule is extended, one stated), how a landed predecessor is found at P is specified, and a /1 predecessor is accepted or refused explicitly; §4.6 is made consistent.
criteria.evidence: §4.2 step 1 now says one remaining job is judged by the single-job rule and is not refused for a stale base. §4.6 says the gate finds a landed predecessor by loading its JobFiles from P's tree (as invariant.rs 294 does) and checking that its fingerprint equals fingerprint(P; R). It says explicitly that a /1 predecessor is accepted. The two partly-landed cases are merged into one, and the tests in §5 item 4 are updated to match.

criteria.criterion: The design resolves R2-m1 (merge-commit refusal message: either note that the existing merge message is shown or list a change to check that passes landing's reason through, with a test) and notes rules changes in R2-n1.
criteria.evidence: §4.3 and §4.6 now say that for a merge commit, check shows the existing message 'a merge introduces governed content that neither parent has'. I confirmed this at invariant.rs 126-138. §5 item 4 adds a test that asserts the message check actually shows. The 'Parent moved' case in §4.6 now names a rules-file change on the base branch, which answers R2-n1.

criteria.criterion: §5 items 1 and 2 name AnyRecord, the schema-name table, the consumers (athena-core run.rs, store.rs, athena-gate jobs.rs), and put RecordSet::load in athena-gate.
criteria.evidence: §5 item 1 names AnyRecord (lines 796-824), the schema-name table (line 914), RecordSet::load in crates/athena-gate/src/records.rs, and the consumers run.rs 950-956, store.rs 145 and jobs.rs 64. Item 2 names run.rs 456-465. A search confirmed the matches at run.rs 953, store.rs 145, jobs.rs 64 and records.rs 914.

criteria.criterion: D69 in docs/decisions.md and the CHANGELOG entry are updated to reflect the answers; D69 stays proposed and no code or tests change; the build is left as a separate later job.
criteria.evidence: D69's Decision now has an 'After review 2' sentence and still begins 'Proposed, awaiting the user's acceptance'. The CHANGELOG has a new entry that ends 'Documentation only; the build is a later job.' The diff stat lists only five .md files.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test` and `cargo fmt --check`: both pass (the repository's wording scan covers the docs).
criteria.evidence: cargo fmt --check printed nothing and exited 0. Every cargo test suite reported ok with 0 failed, including tests/policy.rs (8 passed, among them athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where) and athena_gate (50 passed).

findings.summary: The consumer list in §5 item 1 misses some AnyRecord::Candidate match sites.
findings.evidence: A search also finds AnyRecord::Candidate at crates/athena-core/src/store.rs:187, crates/athena-data/src/records.rs:887 (the canonical path) and crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs:80. The design says the list may be incomplete and that the build job searches again, so this is not a contradiction.

findings.summary: Accepting a /1 predecessor can be misread against D69's Consequences text.
findings.evidence: D69 still says 'Jobs landed before the fields exist cannot form a chain', while §4.6 now accepts a landed /1 predecessor. §4.6 explains that the rule applies only to members of `jobs`, but D69 itself was not clarified.

findings.summary: The edited §4.2 step 4 line and the §4.1 schema line run past the surrounding wrap width.
findings.evidence: The added '(in `athena-gate`)' and '(found as in 4.6, partly landed chains)' make those lines longer than their neighbours. This is the same kind of issue R2-n2 raised.

summary: The candidate does what the accepted reading asks. It answers review 2 of the squash-chain landing design and leaves the build to a later job. It adds Appendix B, which gives each of the six findings a disposition and links the section that changed. It also revises §4.1, §4.2 step 1, §4.3, §4.6 and §5, and amends D69 (which stays proposed), the changelog, and the pointers in two other docs. No code or test changed, and the review file is untouched. I checked the design's code claims against the source. invariant.rs 126-138 does report the generic merge message, line 294 loads `before` from the parent, and run.rs 1145-1195 shows the core lands a job by advancing the branch it works on. That last point means "latest landed job in the base commit's history" names the earlier job when jobs are stacked on a pull-request branch. `AnyRecord::Candidate` is matched at run.rs 953, store.rs 145 and jobs.rs 64, and the schema name is set at records.rs 914. I ran `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo test` and both passed. There are only minor and nit findings: the consumer list in §5 misses a few match sites, though the design says so, and some smaller wording and wrapping issues.
